preamble: Backing of the alveolar tap [ɾ] to a voiced uvular fricative [ʁ]. In Rio de Janeiro (Carioca) Portuguese the coda rhotic, which is a tap [ɾ] in European Portuguese, is realized as a guttural sound, most often voiced ([ʁ], [ɣ], [ɦ]) unlike in other Brazilian regions. The French and German 'guttural R' shifts started from an alveolar trill and belong to the r > ʁ cell.

examples.note: European Portuguese keeps the coda tap (/ˈveɾ.dɨ/). In Rio the coda rhotic is realized as a velar, uvular or glottal fricative; voiced variants such as [ʁ] predominate (phonetically also [ɦ]).
